prompt_text:
Act as a cybersecurity threat intelligence annotation specialist.
From the provided input text, identify named entities using EXCLUSIVELY the following four categories:
- Vulnerability: ONLY an explicit CVE identifier formatted as CVE-YYYY-NNNN (e.g., CVE-2021-44228). Known vulnerability names (like "Log4Shell", "Snake", "EternalBlue") or non-CVE descriptions MUST NOT be labeled as Vulnerabilities, even if they denote a known flaw. Only verbatim CVE-YYYY-NNNN strings qualify for this category.
- Weakness: an explicit CWE identifier (e.g., CWE-89) or a core flaw mechanism.
- Configuration: a specific product, software, component, device, or CPE identifier that may be impacted by vulnerabilities. Generic filenames, IP addresses, ports, or arbitrary strings that are not identifiable affected products/components MUST NOT be treated as Configuration (e.g., "comadmin.dat", "104.155.149[.]103", "443", "winds.exe" are excluded unless clearly given as a product/component name).
- AttackTechnique: a MITRE ATT&CK technique ID or sub-technique ID in the form Txxxx or Txxxx.xxx (e.g., T1190, T1090.002, T1078, T0859, T1021.001) or a clearly named attack technique. Extract every distinct ID occurrence as its own entity using solely the exact ID substring (e.g., from "Valid Accounts (T1078, ICS T0859)" extract "T1078" and "T0859" separately, not the whole phrase; the "ICS " prefix MUST be removed and only the T-code "T0859" is taken). Sub-technique IDs (e.g., T1090.002) and parent technique IDs (e.g., T1090) are both valid when explicitly present. CRITICAL: MITRE ATT&CK TACTIC IDs formatted as TAxxxx (e.g., TA0009, TA0010, TA0011) are OUT OF SCOPE and MUST NOT be extracted as AttackTechnique or any other type. ICS-prefixed technique mentions (e.g., "ICS T0859") ARE IN SCOPE: extract only the exact T-code token (e.g., "T0859") and discard the "ICS " prefix.

Constraints:
1. Each entity text MUST be an exact verbatim substring from the input text. For AttackTechnique entities from ICS-prefixed mentions, the entity text is the T-code token exactly as written in the input (e.g., "T0859" from "ICS T0859"); start and end offsets must map to that T-code substring in the input.
2. Provide 0-based start and end character offsets relative to the input text. end is exclusive, so text[start:end] equals the entity text precisely.
3. For normalized_id, supply the canonical identifier if present (e.g., standard CVE ID, CWE-xxx, canonical CPE 2.3 URI for products, or T-code for ATT&CK); otherwise null.
4. Do not emit repeated duplicate entries for the identical mention span.
5. Extract only entities satisfying the strict definitions above. Omit any span that does not clearly fit one of the four types per these rules.
6. For AttackTechnique, extract only the exact ID token (e.g., "T1090.002", "T1078", "T0859") as entity text, never surrounding description or tactic IDs (TAxxxx).
7. Tactic IDs (TAxxxx) are never extracted. ICS-prefixed technique IDs are extracted as their bare T-code token with accurate offsets.

<text>
Attackers exploited CVE-2021-44228 in the Log4j component to gain initial access by exploiting a public-facing application (T1190).
</text>
<entities>
[
  {"id": "E1", "text": "CVE-2021-44228", "type": "Vulnerability", "start": 20, "end": 34, "normalized_id": "CVE-2021-44228"},
  {"id": "E2", "text": "Log4j", "type": "Configuration", "start": 42, "end": 47, "normalized_id": "cpe:2.3:a:apache:log4j:*:*:*:*:*:*:*:*"},
  {"id": "E3", "text": "T1190", "type": "AttackTechnique", "start": 124, "end": 129, "normalized_id": "T1190"}
]
</entities>
</example>

Act as a cyber threat intelligence annotation specialist.
Identify named entities in the provided text using EXCLUSIVELY these four categories:
- Vulnerability: a precise CVE identifier (e.g., CVE-YYYY-NNNN).
- Weakness: a precise CWE identifier (e.g., CWE-89) OR a commonly accepted flaw class name explicitly described as a vulnerability category (e.g., "server-side request forgery", "SQL injection"). Only extract Weakness entities if (a) a CWE-xxx identifier is present verbatim in the text, or (b) a widely known flaw type name is explicitly stated as a vulnerability class. Do NOT infer, guess, or normalize descriptive vulnerability phrases (such as "improper authentication", "missing authentication check", "buffer overflow condition") into Weakness entities unless they are established flaw category names. If no CWE ID or explicit recognized flaw class exists, return no Weakness entities.
- Configuration: an actual product, software, component, device, or CPE identifier that could be affected by vulnerabilities. This covers multi-word product/component names even when followed by version strings or descriptive parentheticals in the text. When a component name appears with a version or descriptive parenthetical (e.g., "Telerik UI for ASP.NET AJAX Q2 2013 SP1 (version 2013.2.717)"), the Configuration entity is the base product/component name verbatim as written in the text up to the version or descriptive boundary (e.g., extract "Telerik UI for ASP.NET AJAX" from that example, not the version). Do NOT extract known offensive security tools or utilities (e.g., Impacket, KerberCache, RomCom RAT, Meterpreter, S0508, S1063) as Configuration regardless of capitalization or context; these are NEVER Configuration entities.
- AttackTechnique: a MITRE ATT&CK technique ID (e.g., T1190, T1190.002, TA0011) or clearly named attack method.

Constraints:
1. The entity text must be copied verbatim as a substring from the source text.
2. Supply 0-based start and end character offsets based on the input text. End is exclusive so that text[start:end] equals the entity text exactly.
3. For normalized_id, provide the canonical identifier when feasible (e.g., official CVE ID, CWE-xxx, canonical CPE 2.3 URI for products, or T-code for ATT&CK); if unavailable, use null.
4. Do not repeat the same mention span (identical text, start, and end) as duplicate entries.
5. AttackTechnique IDs: Capture EVERY distinct explicit MITRE ATT&CK identifier string (covering technique IDs like T1190, sub-technique IDs like T1190.002, tactic IDs like TA0011, and ICS technique IDs like T0859) as an INDIVIDUAL entity. The entity text must be solely the ID token (e.g., "T1090", "T1090.002", "T1078", "T0859", "TA0011"), not the accompanying description (e.g., NOT "Valid Accounts (T1078, ICS T0859)"). Do NOT extract software/tool names (e.g., S0508, S1063, S0357) as AttackTechnique entities; only extract MITRE ATT&CK T-code or TA-code identifiers.
6. Parent/child or overlapping technique IDs: When both a parent ID and a sub-technique ID appear explicitly and overlap (e.g., "T1090.002" includes "T1090"), extract EACH distinct ID string as a separate entity with its own offsets, even if spans overlap. For instance: from "(T1090.002)" extract "T1090" (start at T, end after T1090) and "T1090.002" (start at T, end after 002) as two entities. NOTE: Only extract the explicitly written ID tokens. Do NOT synthesize a parent ID (e.g., "T1090") from a sub-technique (e.g., "T1090.003") unless the parent ID string appears verbatim as its own token in the text.
7. Do not classify IP addresses, file names, tool names, ports, or similar as Configuration unless they are explicitly a product, software, component, device, or CPE identifier vulnerable to exploits. Generic indicators (e.g., 104.155.149[.]103, winds.exe, 443) are NOT Configuration entities. Known offensive tools/utilities (e.g., Impacket, KerberCache, RomCom RAT) are NEVER Configuration entities. Extract the specific product/software/component name verbatim as it appears up to any version string or descriptive parenthetical boundary (e.g., "Telerik UI for ASP.NET AJAX" from "Telerik UI for ASP.NET AJAX Q2 2013 SP1"); do not append version strings or descriptive phrases to the entity unless the version is part of the official product name in text.
8. If no entities of the permitted types exist, output an empty list.
